name: thin-results
about: Results exist but each rests on one or two leads: too thin to steer by.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

subject_matter.in_our_words: A small fleet where dispatch knows your name

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.
Our ads with hook straight_talk (straight talk) and scene cab_pov (from the cab) spent $41.20 in the last 28 days over 3010 impressions and brought 1 lead, $41.20 per lead.
Our ads with hook proof (proof) and scene equipment_at_rest (truck at rest) spent $38.75 in the last 28 days over 2890 impressions and brought 2 leads, $19.38 per lead.

output.audience: Class A drivers with flatbed experience who meet the experience requirement and want Midwest regional lanes. They likely run longer stretches out or drive for a large fleet. A plain pay per mile, the home-time schedule and an assigned truck would make them stop.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per mile, stated plainly on a plain background with flatbed and Midwest lanes beside it.
angles.proof: The opening states the pay per mile and offers a retirement plan.
angles.why: Pay is the most concrete fact on the opening and no earlier ad of ours has led with it. Nothing has been measured for this hook, so it is a test.

angles.idea: Lead with the home-time schedule, pictured as an ordinary home street at the end of a regional run.
angles.proof: The opening offers the stated home-time schedule on regional Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Home time is what separates a regional job from over-the-road work. No earlier ad of ours has tested a life hook, so this is unmeasured.

angles.idea: Lead with the assigned truck and the flatbed work, shown as a loaded flatbed running a Midwest road.
angles.proof: The job is flatbed with an assigned truck on Midwest lanes.
angles.why: Flatbed drivers choose jobs by the equipment and the work, and an assigned truck is a concrete fact. This hook has no results yet.

angles.idea: State plainly who the job is for: Class A, the experience requirement, flatbed, Midwest lanes, seen from the driver's seat.
angles.proof: The opening states the licence class, the experience requirement, flatbed and Midwest lanes.
angles.why: This pair brought very few leads at a cost near the benchmark's pause line, which is too thin to judge. Stating the requirement plainly should keep unqualified drivers from clicking.

angles.idea: Show the small fleet as the proof: a parked assigned truck and the line that dispatch knows the driver by name.
angles.proof: The carrier describes itself as a small fleet where dispatch knows your name, and the truck is assigned.
angles.why: This pair had the lower cost per lead of our earlier ads, but over very few leads, so it is a lead to follow and not proof. The small-fleet fact gives it something specific to show.
